<problem>
Let \(g\geq2\) be an integer, and set
\[
r=\left\lfloor\frac{g+2}{3}\right\rfloor,\qquad k=g-r.
\]
Let \(C_g\) be the smooth projective completion over \(\mathbb C\) of the affine curve
\[
z^2=x^{2g+1}-1,
\]
and let \(p\) be its unique point over infinity. Choose the local parameter \(t\) at \(p\) satisfying
\[
x=t^{-2},\qquad z=t^{-(2g+1)}(1-t^{4g+2})^{1/2},
\]
where the square root has value \(1\) at \(t=0\).

For a nonzero vector \(b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{r-1})\in\mathbb C^r\), define
\[
\phi_b(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}b_jt^{-(2g-1-2j)}.
\]
Choose coordinate discs \(W_0\Subset W\) centered at \(p\), with \(t\) defined on a neighborhood of \(\overline W\), and put \(U=C_g\setminus\overline{W_0}\). Take product neighborhoods of the zero sections over \(U\) and \(W\), with fiber coordinates \(y_U\) and \(y_W\). After shrinking the fiber directions, glue them over \(U\cap W\), preserving the base point, by
\[
y_W=t^{-1}y_U\bigl(1+k\phi_b(t)y_U^k\bigr)^{-1/k}.
\]
The fractional power denotes the holomorphic branch whose value is \(1\) at \(y_U=0\).

Let \(X_b\) be the resulting smooth analytic surface germ along its zero section \(E\simeq C_g\). Its normal bundle is \(\mathcal O_{C_g}(-p)\), and contracting \(E\) gives a normal surface singularity \((V_b,0)\) with minimal good resolution \(f_b:(X_b,E)\to(V_b,0)\). For cohomology, take \(X_b\) to be the inverse image of a sufficiently small Stein representative of this singularity.

Write \(\mathcal I_E\) for the ideal sheaf of \(E\), and define the logarithmic tangent sheaf by
\[
S_b=\{D\in\Theta_{X_b}:D(\mathcal I_E)\subseteq\mathcal I_E\},
\]
where \(\Theta_{X_b}\) is the sheaf of holomorphic vector fields. Put \(L_b=\bigwedge^2S_b\) and \(h^1(X_b,\mathcal F)=\dim_{\mathbb C}H^1(X_b,\mathcal F)\). Determine the exact formula, as a function of \(g\) and the entire coefficient vector \(b\), for
\[
\Delta_b=h^1(X_b,\mathcal O_{X_b})-h^1(X_b,S_b)+h^1(X_b,L_b),
\]
for every allowed nonzero \(b\), including vectors with vanishing components.
</problem>

A complete answer to this problem: A complete answer is an exact formula or explicit finite rule for the integer Δ_b in terms of g and the entire coefficient vector b, valid for every integer g ≥ 2 and every nonzero b ∈ ℂ^r. Any case distinctions must cover all allowed vectors, including those with vanishing components.

15	## 1. The relevant bundles and transitions
16	
17	Write

19	d=2g-2,\qquad \mathcal F=\ker(S_b\longrightarrow\pi^*\Theta_{C_g}),
20	\qquad \mathcal P=\pi^*\Theta_{C_g},

28	\]

30	Set \(u=y_U,\ v=y_W\), and introduce
31	\[
32	\psi=t^k\phi_b,\qquad B=1-k\psi v^k.
33	\]
34	The inverse fiber-coordinate change is
35	\[
36	u=tvB^{-1/k}.                                                        \tag{2}
37	\]

39	\[
40	u\partial_u=B\,v\partial_v.                                         \tag{3}
41	\]
42	
43	The differential \(dx/z\) has divisor \(dp\). Its dual vector field
44	\[
45	e=z\partial_x+\frac{2g+1}{2}x^{2g}\partial_z
46	\]
47	is a nowhere-zero frame of \(\Theta_{C_g}\) away from \(p\). In the \(t\)-coordinate,
48	\[
49	e=q(t)\partial_t,\qquad
50	q(t)=-\frac12t^{-d}(1-t^{4g+2})^{1/2}.                               \tag{4}
51	\]

53	Let \(\mathcal I=\mathcal I_E\). The associated graded bundles are
54	\[
55	\begin{aligned}
56	\mathcal I^n\mathcal O/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal O
57	 &\simeq\mathcal O_{C_g}(np),\\
58	\mathcal I^n\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F
59	 &\simeq\mathcal O_{C_g}(np),\\
60	\mathcal I^n\mathcal P/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal P
61	 &\simeq\mathcal O_{C_g}((n-d)p),\\
62	\mathcal I^nL_b/\mathcal I^{n+1}L_b
63	 &\simeq\mathcal O_{C_g}((n-d)p).
64	\end{aligned}                                                       \tag{5}
65	\]

67	These filtrations can be used to compute the actual analytic cohomology. Indeed, the first cohomology of the graded terms vanishes for \(n\ge2g-1\) in the first two cases, and for \(n\ge4g-3\) in the last two. The same latter bound applies to \(S_b\), by (1). Formal functions, together with cohomological dimension at most one for a resolution over a sufficiently small Stein representative, therefore gives
68	\[
69	H^1(X_b,\mathcal G)
70	 \simeq H^1(X_b,\mathcal G/\mathcal I^{\,4g-3}\mathcal G)              \tag{6}
71	\]
72	for every sheaf used below. It also gives
73	\[
74	H^1(X_b,\mathcal I^{d+1}\mathcal F)=0.                               \tag{7}
75	\]
76	For clarity, the vanishing assertion follows by first applying the graded vanishing to every finite thickening. Formal functions makes the completion of the corresponding \(R^1f_*\) zero; coherence and Nakayama then make \(R^1f_*\) itself zero.

78	## 2. Scalar obstruction maps
79	
80	The Weierstrass semigroup at \(p\) is
81	\[
82	\langle2,2g+1\rangle.
83	\]
84	Its gaps are \(1,3,\ldots,2g-1\). Thus, for \(m\ge0\),
85	\[
86	H^1(C_g,\mathcal O(mp))
87	 =
88	\left\langle[t^{-\ell}]:
89	 \ell\ \text{odd},\ m<\ell\le2g-1\right\rangle.                      \tag{8}
90	\]
91	In particular, this cohomology has only odd principal-part parity. For \(0\le m\le d\),
92	\[
93	H^0(C_g,\mathcal O(mp))
94	 =\langle1,x,\ldots,x^{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\rangle,                    \tag{9}
95	\]
96	so its elements have even parity.
97	
98	After removing the even holomorphic unit in (4), the four scalar transitions in fiber degree \(n\) have the following form:
99	\[
100	\begin{array}{c|c|c}
101	\text{sheaf}&\text{graded bundle}&\text{factor involving }B\\ \hline
102	\mathcal O&\mathcal O(np)&B^{-n/k}\\
103	\mathcal F&\mathcal O(np)&B^{1-n/k}\\
104	\mathcal P&\mathcal O((n-d)p)&B^{-n/k}\\
105	L_b&\mathcal O((n-d)p)&B^{1-n/k}.
106	\end{array}                                                        \tag{10}
107	\]
108	
109	Expanding \(B^\alpha\) shows that the first possible obstruction raises fiber degree by \(k\). On the corresponding graded cohomology it is multiplication by \(\phi_b\), with scalar coefficient
110	\[
111	n\quad\text{for }\mathcal O,\mathcal P,
112	\qquad
113	n-k\quad\text{for }\mathcal F,L_b.                                  \tag{11}
114	\]
115	Signs do not matter for its rank.
116	
117	### Why there are no further rank losses
118	
119	Here are the details needed to rule out hidden higher obstructions.
120	
121	The transitions preserve fiber degree modulo \(k\), so subsequent obstructions can only raise degree by \(2k,3k,\ldots\). Reindex a possible source by \(m=n\) for \(\mathcal O,\mathcal F\), and by \(m=n-d\) for \(\mathcal P,L_b\). A source capable of reaching nonzero \(H^1\) has \(m\ge0\), and its leading coefficient is even by (9).
122	
123	The function \(\phi_b\) is odd. If the first obstruction vanishes, its correcting cochains can be chosen odd: the ordinary line-bundle Čech decomposition respects the involution \(t\mapsto-t\). The obstruction at the next step, of size \(2k\), is consequently even. It vanishes by (8).
124	
125	Moreover,
126	\[
127	3k\ge d.                                                          \tag{12}
128	\]
129	Indeed \(g\in\{3r-2,3r-1,3r\}\), and \(3k-d=g-3r+2\in\{0,1,2\}\).
130	Thus an obstruction of size \(3k\) is possible only when \(3k=d\) and \(m=0\).
131	
132	For \(\mathcal F,\mathcal P,L_b\), that unique source is already killed by the first obstruction. Its scalar coefficient is respectively \(-k,d,d-k\), all nonzero, and
133	\[
134	[\phi_b]\ne0\quad\text{in }H^1(C_g,\mathcal O(kp)).                   \tag{13}
135	\]
136	To see (13), every monomial of \(\phi_b\) is an odd gap principal part, with pole order at least
137	\[
138	2g-1-2(r-1)=2k+1>k.
139	\]
140	For \(\mathcal O\), the \(m=0\) source is the constant function, which lifts exactly. No larger obstruction is possible.
141	
142	Finally, the exceptional first coefficient \(n-k=0\) for \(\mathcal F\) causes no later obstruction: in that degree the factor in (10) is exactly \(B^0=1\).
143	
144	Therefore all four scalar cohomologies are obtained from their graded cohomologies by subtracting precisely the ranks of the first maps (11).
145	
146	## 3. Comparing the scalar cohomologies
147	
148	For \(m\ge0\), denote by
149	\[
150	R_m=\operatorname{rank}\left(
151	H^0(C_g,\mathcal O(mp))
152	 \xrightarrow{\ \phi_b\ }
153	H^1(C_g,\mathcal O((m+k)p))
154	\right).                                                          \tag{14}
155	\]
156	
157	The sheaves \(\mathcal O\) and \(\mathcal F\) have identical graded bundles. Their first-map ranks agree except in degrees \(0\) and \(k\). Equation (11) therefore gives
158	\[
159	h^1(\mathcal F)-h^1(\mathcal O)=R_k-R_0.                             \tag{15}
160	\]
161	By (13), \(R_0=1\).
162	
163	Put
164	\[
165	s=j(b)+1.
166	\]
167	We claim \(R_k=s\). In the bases (8)–(9), the matrix in (14) for \(m=k\) is
168	\[
169	H=(b_{\ell+a})_{\substack{0\le\ell\le r-1\\
170	                          0\le a\le\lfloor k/2\rfloor}},
171	\qquad b_j=0\quad(j\ge r).                                         \tag{16}
172	\]
173	There are at least \(r\) columns, since \(\lfloor k/2\rfloor+1\ge r\).
174	All entries with \(\ell+a\ge s\) vanish, while the leading \(s\times s\)
175	block is anti-triangular with anti-diagonal \(b_{s-1}\ne0\). Its determinant is
176	\[
177	\pm b_{s-1}^{\,s}.
178	\]
179	All rows and columns beyond that block are zero. Hence \(R_k=s\), proving
180	\[
181	h^1(\mathcal F)=h^1(\mathcal O)+s-1.                                \tag{17}
182	\]
183	
184	Likewise, \(\mathcal P\) and \(L_b\) have identical graded bundles. Every possible \(H^0\) source has fiber degree \(n\ge d\), and both coefficients \(n\) and \(n-k\) in (11) are nonzero. Their first-map ranks, and hence their cohomology dimensions, agree:
185	\[
186	h^1(\mathcal P)=h^1(L_b).                                          \tag{18}
187	\]
188	
189	## 4. The connecting homomorphism is zero
190	
191	It remains important not to discard the connecting homomorphism in (1).
192	
193	Every global section of \(\mathcal P\) has fiber order at least \(d\), because its lower graded bundles have negative degree. A section with a nonzero symbol in degree \(d\) would have first obstruction
194	\[
195	d[\phi_b]\in H^1(C_g,\mathcal O(kp)),
196	\]
197	which is nonzero by (13). Consequently every global section actually belongs to
198	\[
199	H^0(X_b,\mathcal I^{d+1}\mathcal P).
200	\]
201	By (7) and the sequence (1) tensored with \(\mathcal I^{d+1}\), every such section lifts to \(S_b\). Thus the connecting map
202	\[
203	H^0(X_b,\mathcal P)\longrightarrow H^1(X_b,\mathcal F)
204	\]
205	is zero. Since \(H^2(X_b,\mathcal F)=0\), we obtain
206	\[
207	h^1(S_b)=h^1(\mathcal F)+h^1(\mathcal P).                            \tag{19}
208	\]
209	
210	Combining (17)–(19),
211	\[
212	\begin{aligned}
213	\Delta_b
214	 &=h^1(\mathcal O)-h^1(S_b)+h^1(L_b)\\
215	 &=h^1(\mathcal O)-h^1(\mathcal F)\\
216	 &=1-s=-j(b),
217	\end{aligned}
218	\]
219	as asserted. The anti-triangular argument explicitly includes all patterns of vanishing components.
220	
221	## 5. Exact computational verification
222	
223	The following standalone Python uses only rational arithmetic. It **does not compute the cohomology by substituting the answer**: it constructs finite Čech matrices for \(\mathcal O,S_b,L_b\) from the given gluing and computes their ranks.

225	For completeness, the horizontal logarithmic transition used in the code is
226	\[
227	e_U=q\partial_t+
228	q\left(-\frac1t-\phi_b't^kv^k\right)v\partial_v,                    \tag{20}
229	\]
230	together with (2)–(4).
231	
232	Here is why its Laurent cutoffs are certified. Set \(N=4g-3\) and
233	\[
234	R_n=3n+4g.
235	\]
236	Retain the negative Laurent rows \(t^ev^n\) with \(-R_n\le e<0\); for the vertical component of \(S_b\), retain one additional row. A basis of functions regular away from \(p\), indexed by pole order, is
237	\[
238	a_D=
239	\begin{cases}
240	x^{D/2},&D\text{ even},\\
241	x^{(D-2g-1)/2}z,&D\text{ odd},\ D\ge2g+1.
242	\end{cases}
243	\]
244	The respective source cutoffs in degree \(n\) are
245	\[
246	D\le4n+4g,\qquad
247	D\le4n+2g+2,\qquad
248	D\le4n+4g+1
249	\]
250	for \(\mathcal O\), for \(L_b\) or the horizontal component, and for the vertical component.
251

Every omitted target monomial corresponds to a nongap pole order and can be eliminated by an omitted source. Analytic rather than polynomial source functions introduce no extra relations: a source whose boundary has finite principal parts extends meromorphically at \(p\), degree by degree.
